answer: Agents can earn a nontransferable reputation by completing repeated trades that counterparties later attest to; each new account starts with no history and must post a bond that is forfeited for proven fraud. A basalt supplier might build trust at a harbor by delivering umber ore across many independently chosen partners. Splitting into sybils does not split the bond or create attestations: the attacker must lock up fresh capital and repeat costly deliveries for every identity, while colluding accounts’ circular endorsements carry little weight.
